Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking a look at our draft DPA addendum. Two narrow items are blocking procurement: (1) the exact service-provider / processor language under CCPA/CPRA — we need a clear statement that Redwood will act as a ‘service provider’ (i.e., no sale of personal information, limited use only) and (2) the onshore fallback for telemetry and logs in case of cross-border constraints (we need an explicit fallback to US-hosted processing if required for audits).

Can you confirm whether you can accept our proposed paragraph about the "no sale" commitment and if Redwood will provide a maintained subprocessor registry with 30-day notice for new subprocessors? I attached a suggested redline (CPRA_Addendum_SuggestedEdits.pdf) and our standard checklist.

Laura — thanks for the clear callouts and the redline. Short answers up front: yes on the service provider / "no sale" commitment; yes on a publicly maintainable subprocessor registry with 30-day notice for new subprocessors; and yes on an onshore fallback for telemetry for audit/regulated workflows, subject to a scoped operational playbook.

Couple of caveats we should align on before finalizing language:
- Telemetry definition: we'd like to agree on a bounded set (telemetry = host/instance metrics, request latencies, aggregated KPIs) vs. customer PD (user content). We'll propose a short definition to avoid overbroad commitments.
- Onshore fallback: we can commit to an onshore processing path for telemetry and audit artifacts, but it requires cooperation on timing and a short lead time (we typically need 48–72 hours to redirect pipelines and enable onshore retention).
- Subprocessor notices: Redwood publishes a live registry and can provide email notice 30 days before onboarding a new subprocessor; for emergency security-required subprocessors we can provide quicker notice and a documented escalation.

I'll loop in Ben (legal ops / deals) to confirm the exact DPA phrasing and to propose a clean redline back. If Silverline wants, we can also run the final addendum by our outside counsel (Tom) for a one-hour pass.

Will share a proposed redline by tomorrow EOD.

— Ava Chen

Ava / Marissa — forwarding Laura's thread and Ava's note. I'm attaching a quick proposed snippet we can offer that is intentionally limited but should satisfy Silverline procurement: short service-provider clause, explicit no-sale, a telemetry definition, 48–72 hour onshore fallback SLA, and subprocessor registry + 30-day notice. See bullets below for the redline we plan to include.

Proposed redline (high level):
- Service provider clause: "For the purposes of the CCPA/CPRA, Redwood Inference shall act as a 'Service Provider' and shall not sell, rent, or otherwise disclose personal information except as necessary to provide services under the Agreement and subject to the limited use restrictions set forth herein."
- No-sale commitment: "Redwood certifies it will not 'sell' personal information as defined under applicable US state privacy laws."
- Telemetry definition + handling: "Telemetry: aggregate and system-level metrics, request/throughput logs, and diagnostic traces that do not contain customer content or user-generated personal data. Telemetry will be pseudonymized and retained per the retention schedule in the DPA. If required for regulatory audit, Redwood will enable an onshore processing fallback within 48–72 hours for telemetry and audit logs for the customer account."
- Subprocessor registry: "Redwood maintains a live subprocessor registry (link). Redwood will provide email notice 30 days prior to onboarding new subprocessors; in emergency scenarios Redwood will provide notice as practicable and documented mitigation steps."

Action items: Ava — can you send the proposed redline to Laura and copy Tom? Marissa — please validate the 48–72 hour operational commitment with infra runbooks / oncall to ensure we can meet it for Silverline's tier.

Ben Carter
